target.title: fix(browser): normalize local dispatch request paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The in-process browser route dispatcher normalized request paths differently from the node/browser proxy path. Local dispatch accepted missing leading slashes, but did not trim whitespace or strip trailing slashes the same way the shared browser request policy does.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser request entry points should route and guard the same normalized path. This change reuses `normalizeBrowserRequestPath` in the local dispatcher instead of keeping a narrower local normalizer.

## User Impact

Local browser request dispatch now behaves consistently with node-host browser requests for paths such as `snapshot`, `/snapshot/`, and `  snapshot/  `. Existing guarded route checks continue to use the same normalized path contract.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/dispatcher.ts`.
- Added `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/dispatcher.path-normalization.test.ts` to prove local dispatch path normalization matches proxy request behavior.
- Live open-PR conflict scan found no exact overlap on these touched files.

## Proof

- Rebased cleanly onto `upstream/main` at `fbcb7812cb`.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/dispatcher.path-normalization.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/dispatcher.abort.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.test.ts`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Earlier touched-file checks: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 ...`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json ...`, and Claude autoreview clean after Codex autoreview was blocked by local OpenAI API 401.
